title: Wii Party
subtitle: The Miis become the party guests
summary: Wii Party is NDcube's Wii multiplayer collection placing the players' Mii characters inside board games, paired challenges and activities that extend into the living room. Its different modes draw on a large set of minigames, giving friends several ways to organise the same gathering. body: Wii Party is NDcube's Wii multiplayer collection placing the players' Mii characters inside board games, paired challenges and activities that extend into the living room. Its different modes draw on a large set of minigames, giving friends several ways to organise the same gathering. The familiar avatars make the competitors recognisable without requiring a licensed cast. A session can follow a board toward a final result or turn toward a shorter activity, allowing the group to choose how much structure it wants around the next shared game.

House Party activities pay attention to the people and controllers outside the television. Rather than keeping every task inside a virtual board, they use the group's surroundings and the ways a Remote can be handled or passed between players. Party Games and Pair Games provide other arrangements, including more conventional contests and challenges built around two participants. The categories give the collection different social shapes. A change of mode can alter who cooperates, who competes and how much of the action depends on watching the people in the room.

Most modes incorporate minigames that communicate their task quickly and return a result before the group loses track of the wider contest. The collection also allows its small games to be approached through modes devoted to them. This gives individual favourites a life beyond the board on which they first appeared. NDcube's use of Miis reinforces the connection between the on-screen outcome and the friends taking part, making the next turn another small episode in a gathering whose personalities are already present before the television is switched on.
